data.narrative:
Deepnight, a Seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Lucas Young and Thomas Li, has raised $5.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—two public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and eight private players including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic. This cohort spans Seed through Series A stages within the same sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression, anchored to total capital raised as a proxy for Seed valuation ($6M), applies a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x, yielding $14M. Peer-Median examines five same-sector comparables at matching or adjacent stages, with valuations ranging from $125M (NODA AI, Series A) to $4.0B (Stark Defence, Series A); the median across this set is $1.0B. The wide peer range ($125M–$4.0B) reflects material variation in Defense & Security company maturity, technology differentiation, and customer traction at these stages.

These methods imply a valuation range of $12M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $507M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median reflects Deepnight's nascent funding relative to later-stage comparables. Key uncertainties include whether peer valuations reflect similar technical risk, customer concentration, and regulatory exposure; and whether Deepnight's specific defensibility aligns with higher or lower quartiles within the Defense sector.
